newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Jan-April copper output rises 10 pct on '96.
newsitem.headline: Chile Jan-April copper output rises 10 pct on '96.

text.p: Chile produced 1.06 million tonnes of copper in the first four months of the year, up 10 percent from the same period last year, said state copper studies body Comision Chilena del Cobre (Cochilco).
"It is important to note the more than 50 percent increase in the production of electro-won cathodes obtained through the heap-leaching process," said Cochilco in a report.
Cochilco's figures showed electro-won cathode output climbed to 280,000 tonnes in the January-April period from 184,700 tonnes in the same period 1996.
The steep increase is in large part the result of the start-up last year of the 225,000-tonne El Abra mine, owned by state copper company Codelco and Cyprus Amax Minerals
Output of refined copper produced using the traditional concentrator and smelter rose just one percent to 364,800 tonnes from 361,100 tonnes in the first four months of 1996.
Concentrate output totalled 355,700 tonnes, up three percent from 346,300 tonnes in the January-April period last year.
Copper blister production fell 16.5 percent to 61,200 tonnes.
Export volumes rose 16 percent in the first four months of the year with export income rising 13 percent despite a six percent fall in prices compared with 1996.

Asia continued to be the most important market for Chilean copper, receiving 54 percent of total shipments in the first four months of the year. Japan accounted for 21 percent of exports to the region.
Molybdenum production rose 16 percent to 6,721 tonnes from 5,812 tonnes in the January-April period 1996.
